{
  "research_question": "Do stimulation paradigms (Combined, ICMS Only, Dim Visual Only, Bright Visual Only, Sham) differentially affect mouse navigation performance as measured by Time-to-Target, Success, Path Efficiency, Average Speed, and Angular Dispersion (AD)?",
  "stim_paradigms_compared": ["Combined", "ICMS Only", "Dim Visual Only", "Bright Visual Only", "Sham"],
  "response_variables": ["Time-to-Target", "Success", "Path Efficiency", "Average Speed", "AD"],
  "anova_plan": [
    "Conduct separate one-way ANOVAs for each continuous response variable (Time-to-Target, Path Efficiency, Average Speed, AD) with Stim Paradigm as the 5-level categorical factor",
    "For Success (binary), use logistic regression or chi-square test of independence rather than ANOVA; alternatively, arcsine transformation for proportion data if modeling as continuous",
    "Check ANOVA assumptions: normality of residuals (Shapiro-Wilk or visual inspection), homogeneity of variance (Levene's test), and independence given repeated measures across mice",
    "Given severe imbalance in group sizes (Combined n=48846 vs Sham n=3505), use Type III sums of squares and verify that variance homogeneity holds; consider Welch's ANOVA if variances differ"
  ],
  "posthoc_plan": [
    "For continuous variables meeting ANOVA assumptions: Tukey's HSD or Games-Howell post-hoc tests depending on variance homogeneity",
    "Games-Howell specifically for pairwise comparisons when group variances are unequal or sample sizes are unequal",
    "For Success (binary): pairwise comparisons of proportions with Bonferroni-adjusted z-tests or logistic regression contrasts",
    "Emphasize theoretically meaningful contrasts: Combined vs single-modality conditions, ICMS Only vs Visual conditions, and all active conditions vs Sham"
  ],
  "multiple_comparison_strategy": "Family-wise error rate control via Bonferroni correction across the 5 response variables × 10 pairwise comparisons = 50 tests maximum; for post-hoc within each variable, use Tukey's HSD (built-in FWER control) or Holm-Bonferroni step-down procedure if using custom contrasts; apply Benjamini-Hochberg FDR control as sensitivity analysis given large sample sizes and multiple endpoints",
  "predictive_model_recommendation": "Given that Stim Paradigm is categorical and the goal is prediction (not just inference), recommend multinomial logistic regression with Stim Paradigm as the response variable and the five performance metrics as predictors. This directly models P(Stim Paradigm | performance) and handles the categorical nature appropriately. Alternative: Linear discriminant analysis (LDA) or random forest classifier if nonlinear relationships exist. Avoid ordinary linear regression with Stim Paradigm encoded as numeric; this would impose false ordinality. The multinomial model allows estimation of log-odds ratios for each paradigm relative to a reference (e.g., Sham) and provides classification accuracy metrics.",
  "assumptions_and_diagnostics": [
    "Independence assumption potentially violated: 8 mice contribute multiple trials; must account for clustering via mixed-effects ANOVA or include Mouse as random effect",
    "Normality: Time-to-Target and Path Efficiency show extreme max values (201.39 and 29.82 vs means ~2.8 and 0.47), indicating heavy right skew; log-transformation or robust methods (e.g., permutation ANOVA) may be needed",
    "Homogeneity of variance: Large sample size differences (Combined 48846 vs Sham 3505) make variance estimates unstable in small groups; Levene's test and Welch correction essential",
    "Success is bounded [0,1] with mean 0.73; binary nature violates linear model assumptions",
    "Multicollinearity among predictors: Path Efficiency, Time-to-Target, and Speed likely correlated; check VIF in predictive model",
    "AD range [0.0006, 1.0] with mean 0.38; possible floor/ceiling effects near boundaries"
  ],
  "expected_findings": [
    "Sham condition expected to show poorest performance: lowest Success (0.273), highest Time-to-Target (4.68s), lowest Path Efficiency (0.308), lowest Average Speed (10.74), and lowest AD (0.236)",
    "Combined stimulation expected to outperform single-modality conditions: highest Success (0.780), lowest Time-to-Target (2.56s), high Path Efficiency (0.502), highest Speed (12.83), and highest AD (0.399)",
    "Bright Visual Only expected to perform comparably to Combined, possibly due to optimal visual cue salience (Success 0.785, Time-to-Target 2.61s)",
    "Dim Visual Only and ICMS Only expected intermediate: similar Success (~0.67-0.69), Time-to-Target (~3.0-3.1s), Path Efficiency (~0.43), with Dim Visual showing lower AD (0.336) than ICMS (0.354)",
    "AD pattern suggests angular dispersion tracks stimulation engagement: higher in active/combined conditions, lowest in Sham",
    "Statistical significance highly likely given large n, but effect sizes and confidence intervals will be more informative than p-values"
  ],
  "limitations": [
    "Massive imbalance in group sizes (Combined 63.7% of data, Sham 4.6%) reduces power for Sham comparisons and inflates Type I error risk for small-group variance estimates",
    "Extreme outliers in Time-to-Target (max 201s) and Path Efficiency (max 29.8) suggest data quality issues or rare events; robust methods or outlier exclusion may be necessary",
    "Repeated measures structure ignored in standard ANOVA; 8 mice with varying trial counts (7233-10986) create clustering that can inflate false positive rate",
    "Binary Success variable inappropriate for standard ANOVA; separate analytical framework required",
    "No information on trial order, learning effects, or session structure; temporal confounds possible",
    "AD interpretation as 'angular dispersion' assumes circular statistics knowledge; linear statistics may mischaracterize angular data near 0/1 boundaries",
    "Causal inference limited: Stim Paradigm is experimenter-manipulated, but performance feedback and trial sequence not described"
  ],
  "recommended_next_analysis": "Fit a multinomial logistic mixed-effects model with Stim Paradigm as categorical response, the five performance metrics as fixed-effect predictors (potentially log-transformed for Time-to-Target and Path Efficiency), and Mouse as random intercept; evaluate classification accuracy via cross-validation; supplement with nonparametric permutation ANOVAs for each performance variable to handle outliers and distribution violations; visualize paradigm-specific distributions using violin plots with individual mouse trajectories overlaid to assess within-mouse vs between-mouse variance partitioning."
}
